counterfactual_missing_items: No documented low-voltage ECG or myocardial thickening to support cardiac amyloidosis
No documented systolic dysfunction or wall-motion abnormality to support chemotherapy-induced cardiomyopathy
No raw evidence linking the ECG/laboratory abnormalities specifically to amyloid rather than the atrial mass
decisive_items: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed 4 years ago
diffuse medium masses in the right atrium
significantly increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium and adjacent pericardium
response.rationale: R3 integrates the prior diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with the right atrial mass and pericardial FDG uptake, exactly matching the presenting ECG, biomarker and symptom burden. R4 rests on nonspecific ECG and NT-proBNP findings while ignoring the anatomically targeted echo/PET evidence and lymphoma history. R1 uses only chemotherapy exposure and elevated NT-proBNP, with no supporting imaging substrate.

rejected.why: Only chemotherapy history and elevated NT-proBNP are supportive; the right atrial mass and avid pericardial uptake are unexplained, and no systolic dysfunction or echo correlate is described.
